newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU's Schaeuble says tax reform may be delayed - aide.
newsitem.headline: CDU's Schaeuble says tax reform may be delayed - aide.

text.p: Christian Democrat (CDU) parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble said Germany's planned tax reform may be delayed, a CDU parliamentary spokesman said on Thursday.

One day after the collapse of talks with opposition Social Democrats aimed at reaching a consensus on thorny tax-reform issues, Schaeuble said cuts in corporate taxes may not be ready to start in 1998, but will instead be rolled back into the broader tax reform package planned for 1999, the aide said.
The planned reduction in the solidarity surcharge to 5.5 percent from the current 7.5 percent would still take place on January 1, 1998, he said.
Schaeuble said the delay was due to responses from analysts that the reform would not have a big impact on jobs.
Both the 1998 and 1999 tax bills are due to be passed by the lower house of parliament by early July. Their expected rejection by the upper house will land them in parliament's mediation committee.

Schaeuble said there was still time to discuss cuts in social insurance payments that could take effect in January 1998. The coalition still aims to pass pension reform legislation this year, but implementation will take until 1999, he said.
